area: RegistrationSubmissionFeedback placement after the submit button (diff hunk @@ -324)
issue: In the funnel renderer the feedback (focus target) is rendered after the submit button, while in lead-form it is before the button. After a failed submit, focus moves to the alert, so the sequential-focus starting point is after the button. Keyboard retry then requires Shift+Tab, whereas in lead-form a single Tab reaches the button.
evidence: Funnel renderer: <button type="submit" ...> is followed by <RegistrationSubmissionFeedback .../>; lead-form: <RegistrationSubmissionFeedback/> precedes <button type="submit">. The effect calls alert.focus() when focus is lost or on the submit button.
impact: Inconsistent keyboard retry path between the two real callers; a keyboard user in the funnel form who submitted via the button must navigate backward to retry.
recommended_fix: Either place the feedback before the submit button in the funnel renderer, or, when the active element was the same-form submit button/lost focus, restore focus to the (re-enabled) submit button and rely on the role=alert announcement.
required_test: Browser keyboard test in the funnel renderer: submit via Enter/Space on the button with a failing endpoint, then verify one Tab/Shift+Tab sequence reaches the submit button and that the error is announced once.

issue: Tests use static server markup only, so the useEffect focus-restoration policy (the core behavior of this change) has no automated coverage: body/lost focus, same-form submit button, focus on another field/link preserved, repeated identical error after pending toggle.
evidence: All four tests call renderToStaticMarkup, which does not run effects or touch document.activeElement.
impact: Regressions in the focus policy (e.g. stealing intentional outside focus) would not be caught by unit tests; the user states browser validation is separate, but it is not a repeatable regression guard.
recommended_fix: Add a jsdom/React Testing Library test that renders inside a <form>, toggles pending true->false with the same errorMessage, and asserts document.activeElement for each focus starting point.
required_test: Component tests: (1) activeElement=body -> alert focused; (2) activeElement=form submit button -> alert focused; (3) activeElement=an outside input/link -> unchanged; (4) pending false->true->false with identical errorMessage refocuses again.

issue: If the component were rendered outside a <form>, form is null and any orphan submit button (button.form === null) would satisfy `active.form === form`, causing a focus steal.
evidence: `active.type === "submit" && active.form === form` with form possibly null; HTMLButtonElement.form is null when not in a form.
impact: Not reachable with the two current callers (both inside forms); latent for future reuse.
recommended_fix: Require `form !== null` in the onSubmit condition.
required_test: Unit test rendering the component outside a form with a focused standalone button and asserting focus is not moved.

issue: The old code rendered `message` whenever it was truthy (alert for error, status for any other state). The new code shows it only when status === "error" or "success". Any other status that sets `message` (or status==="error" with an empty message) would now show no feedback.
evidence:
Before: `{message ?

…` ; after: errorMessage={status==="error" ? message : ""} successMessage={status==="success" ? message : ""}. The full status union is not in the supplied scope, and unlike lead-form there is no fallback error message here.
impact: If a third status or an empty error message exists in the renderer, the user would see no result after submit (silent failure), which was previously not the case for non-error statuses.
recommended_fix: Verify the status union in the renderer; if other statuses carry messages, route them to successMessage/errorMessage appropriately, and add a fallback like formSubmissionErrorMessage() for status==="error" with empty message.
required_test: Renderer test enumerating every status value that can set `message` and asserting a visible/announced message for each, including error with empty message.
reason: Current full PublicSubmissionForm has only idle/submitting/success/error. It initializes and clears message to empty before submission, then assigns non-empty messages only for success/error. No other message-bearing status or empty error path exists.
